Lines in the scene (roads, fences) that lead the viewer's eye to the subject.
How much of the image is sharp from front to back. Low f-number = shallow.
The lens opening, shown as f-number, controlling light and depth of field.
How long the sensor is exposed. Fast freezes movement; slow blurs it.
Camera's sensitivity to light. High ISO brightens dark scenes but adds grain.
The low, warm, soft light near sunrise and sunset.
A dark shape against a light background, from backlighting.
A grid of small images of a whole shoot for comparing and selecting.
A camera-less image made by placing objects on light-sensitive paper. Man Ray called his rayographs.
French street photographer known for 'the decisive moment'.
American photographer of black-and-white landscapes with a wide tonal range.
Photographer of staged self-portraits in many roles, exploring identity.

short.q: Explain how light can change a photograph's mood.
short.model: Soft low warm light feels calm; hard side light makes strong shadows and drama; backlight makes silhouettes. Changing time or light direction changes the mood.

short.q: Describe how to make a photograph the start of a drawing or painting.
short.model: Crop to the best composition, print in black and white to study tone, transfer main shapes by sketch or grid, then interpret it in your own way.

short.q: Give two reasons for using your own photographs.
short.model: They are primary sources that show your own observation (AO3) and decisions, and you control viewpoint, light and crop for your intention.

short.q: What does shutter speed do creatively?
short.model: A fast speed freezes movement; a slow speed blurs it, showing motion.

short.q: How can you show AO2 through editing?
short.model: Try several edits such as crop, black and white and contrast, show before and after, and explain which you select and why.
